whatItDoes: Set a limit of three consecutive terms for the 17th Judicial District’s district attorney.
yesMeans: Approve the proposed limit of three consecutive terms.
noMeans: Do not approve this proposed term limit.

whatItDoes: Change Thornton’s charter so a city council member, including the mayor, automatically resigns and vacates office upon formally declaring candidacy for any elected office other than Thornton council member or mayor. Formal declarations include filing a candidate affidavit, petition or other legally required candidacy document.
yesMeans: Approve the automatic-resignation rule for running for another elected office.
noMeans: Do not add this rule to the city charter.

whatItDoes: Raise Northglenn’s sales tax on accommodation services from 5% to 8%, beginning in 2027. It would raise $450,000 annually initially and amounts based on collections later. Revenue could fund general city purposes, including public safety, street maintenance, parks, recreation, culture and administration. Revenue could be collected and spent outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits.
yesMeans: Approve the higher accommodation-services tax and its revenue-limit exception.
noMeans: Do not approve the increase; keep the existing 5% rate on these services.

whatItDoes: Without imposing a new tax, let Westminster Public Schools collect the full education-tax revenue voters approved in 1988, 2002 and 2018, subject to the district’s statutory limit. Money would go into the general fund, in addition to other general-fund property taxes, for previously authorized educational purposes, including safety and security, career and technical education, teachers and student achievement. Investment earnings on these taxes could be collected, kept and spent outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits and other legal limits.
yesMeans: Approve full collection under the earlier tax authorizations and the revenue-limit exception for investment earnings.
noMeans: Do not approve this collection authority or the proposed exception for investment earnings.

whatItDoes: Authorize up to $125 million in Bennett School District 29J bonds, with total repayment capped at $235 million, and up to $11 million in additional property taxes annually to repay them. Projects include a new high school on the existing campus with career and technical education and athletic facilities, converting the current high school to a middle school, and safety, security, lighting, parking and traffic improvements. Other school repairs and improvements could be made as funds allow. A citizens’ oversight committee would monitor spending. The property-tax rate would have no fixed cap but could collect only enough for bond principal and interest, within the stated dollar limits.
yesMeans: Approve the school bonds, property taxes to repay them and citizen spending oversight.
noMeans: Do not authorize these bonds or the related additional property taxes.

whatItDoes: Immediately and permanently repeal all North Range Metropolitan District No. 3 borrowing permissions from earlier voter elections that remain unused.
yesMeans: Repeal the district’s unused debt authorizations.

whatItDoes: Immediately and permanently repeal North Range District 3’s 2014 Ballot Issue 5D, which permits multiyear financial obligations through contracts or agreements funded by up to $280 million in annual property-tax levies. Existing valid and lawful contracts and agreements would be protected. Future multiyear obligations not subject to annual budget approval, or any future funding levies, would need specific voter authorization.
yesMeans: Repeal the 2014 authorization while protecting existing valid agreements and requiring specific voter approval for the stated future obligations and levies.

whatItDoes: Immediately and permanently repeal North Range District 3’s 2014 Ballot Issue 5B, which permits up to $20 million in annual property taxes for capital costs of public improvements. Existing valid and lawful contracts and agreements would be protected. Future capital-financing obligations that do not depend on annual budget approval, or future taxes for new capital improvements, would need specific voter authorization.
yesMeans: Repeal the 2014 authorization, protect existing valid agreements and require specific voter approval for the stated future capital obligations and taxes.

whatItDoes: Reduce North Range District 3’s maximum annual operating and maintenance property-tax authority from $20 million to $9 million. The new cap would adjust annually for inflation using the Colorado Consumer Price Index tracked by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Money would maintain parks and open space, fund district operations and support district public services. The property-tax rate itself would have no fixed cap unless the board sets one, but collections could not exceed the inflation-adjusted dollar limit. Taxes and investment income could be collected and spent in 2026 and later years outside Colorado’s constitutional revenue limits and the statutory property-tax limit.
yesMeans: Approve the lower annual tax-dollar limit, inflation adjustments and revenue-limit exceptions.
noMeans: Do not approve replacing the existing $20 million annual limit with the proposed inflation-adjusted $9 million limit.

whatItDoes: Add a 1% sales tax in Adams County Fire Protection District, raising $11,732,488 in the first full fiscal year and amounts based on collections annually afterward. Exemptions include groceries, gasoline, prescriptions and diapers. Money would support emergency response, staffing, responder health and safety, equipment and training. The tax would be added to other district taxes. Revenue and spending would appear in the annual independent audit online and receive citizen-board review. The district could retain and spend tax revenue above Colorado’s constitutional revenue limit, the statutory property-tax limit and other legal limits.
yesMeans: Approve the additional sales tax, audit and citizen-board review, and revenue-limit exceptions.
noMeans: Do not approve this sales tax or its proposed revenue-limit exceptions.

whatItDoes: Authorize up to $250 million in Central Colorado Water Conservancy District debt, with total repayment capped at $470 million and an effective annual interest rate no higher than 6%. Authorize up to $18.7 million in additional property taxes annually, with a levy no greater than 3 mills except where state law permits. Money would develop and manage water supplies, acquire senior water rights, and build or improve reservoirs and other facilities serving agricultural water needs. Other district revenue could also secure debt payments and reserves. Investment earnings on tax revenue and borrowed money would receive a voter-approved revenue-limit exception.
yesMeans: Approve the water-project borrowing, additional property taxes within the stated limits and the exception for investment earnings.
noMeans: Do not authorize this borrowing, additional taxes or related investment-earnings exception.

whatItDoes: Increase the Groundwater Management Subdistrict’s property taxes by $1.5 million in 2027, with annual inflation increases afterward as defined by Colorado’s constitution. A levy would raise the authorized amounts and put revenue into the subdistrict’s general fund. Money would support water supplies and rights, efficient water delivery, reservoirs and storage facilities, and infrastructure in Adams, Morgan and Weld counties. The measure would approve a revenue change and an exception to the statutory property-tax limit.
yesMeans: Approve the subdistrict property-tax increase, annual inflation adjustments and revenue-limit exception.
noMeans: Do not approve this tax increase or its proposed revenue-limit exception.

whatItDoes: Permanently waive Greater Brighton Fire Protection District’s 5.25% property-tax limit so it can retain previously approved property-tax revenue. Uses include hiring, training and retaining staff, fire and lifesaving equipment, and other operational and capital needs.
yesMeans: Waive the 5.25% property-tax limit for all future property-tax years.

whatItDoes: Create a 0.75% sales tax in Bennett Fire Protection District, raising $1.2 million in the first full fiscal year beginning July 1, 2027, and amounts based on collections annually afterward. It would apply where the state imposes sales tax, with groceries and other exempt items excluded. Money would support fire, ambulance and emergency medical response, rescue and safety services, including facilities and staffing. The district could collect, keep and spend all district revenue despite legal revenue limits.
yesMeans: Approve the sales tax for emergency services and permission to keep and spend district revenue beyond legal limits.
noMeans: Do not approve this sales tax or the proposed revenue-limit exception.

whatItDoes: Without increasing property taxes, permanently waive Bennett Fire Protection District’s 5.25% property-tax limit. The measure would support response times, responder safety and facilities through staffing, training, equipment maintenance and replacement, and fire-station infrastructure and deferred maintenance. It would also allow all district revenue to be collected, kept and spent despite legal revenue limits.
yesMeans: Approve the permanent property-tax-limit waiver and permission to retain and spend district revenue beyond legal limits.
noMeans: Keep the 5.25% property-tax limit and do not approve the proposed revenue-limit exception.
